entities.name: Training lowers intrinsic HR
observations: In 51 adults after 6 months of supervised exercise, resting HR fell 5.2 bpm, while atropine-sensitive and isoproterenol responses were unchanged; authors attributed the fall mainly to reduced intrinsic HR. Intrinsic rate was inferred pharmacologically, not measured by complete blockade.

entities.name: Athlete intrinsic HR lower
observations: Long-term endurance-trained men had approximately 13 bpm lower intrinsic HR than untrained men during rest and exercise after combined autonomic blockade; cross-sectional design and cardiac-volume differences limit causal inference.

entities.name: Intrinsic sinus remodeling
observations: Invasive electrophysiology found longer sinus cycle length in endurance athletes than controls at baseline, after atropine, and after atropine plus propranolol, supporting intrinsic sinus-node remodeling; sample size was 6 per group.

entities.name: Rodent intrinsic bradycardia
observations: Training reduced rat intrinsic HR after autonomic blockade by about 40 bpm in one study; isolated atrial preparations remained slower under blockade in another, while vagal responses were not enhanced. Translation to humans is uncertain.

entities.name: SAN electrical remodeling
observations: In trained mice, bradycardia persisted after autonomic blockade and in denervated SAN preparations, associated with reduced HCN4/funny current; GIRK4-dependent autonomic signaling may trigger or modulate the remodeling.
